entities.summary:
The Battle of Westerplatte was a pivotal first battle in the invasion of Poland, marking the beginning of the Second World War on September 1, 1939. This 7-day siege was a crucial moment in the lead-up to the war, as German forces aimed to capture the strategic peninsula of Westerplatte, a key location for the Polish military. The battle resulted in the deaths of over 200 Polish defenders and 18 German soldiers, a loss that would be avenged by the Poles in the following months.

The Battle of Westerplatte was a landmark moment in the war, as it highlighted the ferocity and determination of the Polish military in the face of overwhelming German odds. The battle also marked the first time German forces would clash with the Polish army in a full-scale conflict. The bravery and sacrifice of the Polish defenders would serve as a rallying cry for the nation and inspire them to continue fighting against the German occupation.

The legacy of the Battle of Westerplatte can be seen in the resilience and patriotism of the Polish people, who would continue to resist German rule throughout the war. The battle also serves as a testament to the importance of preserving historical sites and commemorating the sacrifices of those who fought for their country.

'Wars do not make men savage, they only lay bare the savagery that lies beneath the surface.' – Alexander Solzhenitsyn, reflecting on the brutality of war and the humanity that still managed to exist in the face of it.
